name: What should be included in a bathroom plumbing relocation estimate?

mainEntity.name: What should be included in a bathroom plumbing relocation estimate?
mainEntity.text: What should be included in a bathroom plumbing relocation estimate?

acceptedAnswer.text: A bathroom plumbing relocation estimate should clearly separate the plumbing work from the rebuild work so there are no surprises later. It should list demolition, rerouting of supply and drain lines, vent adjustments, fixture reconnection, permit handling, inspections, and any required slab, framing, or drywall repair. If the project involves a shower or toilet move, the estimate should also note whether waterproofing, tile replacement, or floor restoration are included. Homeowners should look for line items that explain assumptions about access, pipe length, floor construction, and fixture type. A vague lump-sum number is risky because hidden conditions can change the price quickly once walls or floors are opened. The best estimate also states what is excluded, such as cabinetry, custom tile, or finish-grade restoration, so the contractor and homeowner are aligned before work begins.
acceptedAnswer.description: A good estimate should include demolition, pipe rerouting, drain and vent work, shutoff and reconnection, permit handling, inspection coordination, patching, and any slab or framing repair. It should also state what finish restoration is excluded.
